title: AI-informed audience development converted surrounding footfall into modestly higher cultural visitation at a Maltese arts centre
source_unit: Peer-reviewed study of AI-powered footfall monitoring, non-visitor surveys, and audience-development intervention at Spazju Kreattiv, Malta's National Centre for Creativity
geography: Valletta, Malta; Spazju Kreattiv and surrounding public spaces

observations.period: 2025 study; visitor and non-visitor measurement frame

denominator.unit: valid survey respondents combined with continuous anonymized external and internal footfall monitoring

local_residents.unit: survey respondents reporting residence in Malta

nonresident_or_temporary.unit: survey respondents not residing in Malta

measurement_route.value: GDPR-compliant computer-vision sensors measured anonymized pedestrian movement outside the venue and internal visits, while surveys captured awareness, motivations, barriers, and participation context

mechanism.value: Measuring non-visitors alongside visitors makes the conversion problem visible: public proximity is not equivalent to cultural access or participation

observations.method: Peer-reviewed mixed-method case study combining anonymized FlowHint computer-vision monitoring, machine-learning footfall forecasting, survey research, and venue benchmarks.
observations.uncertainty: This is a single-venue case with a non-probability survey and site-specific spatial and social conditions; awareness and footfall are not population estimates or measures of sustained cultural participation.
observations.subgroup: Pedestrians and visitors around Spazju Kreattiv, including Malta residents and international or temporary visitors.
observations.counterinterpretation: Central location and tourism patterns, programming, weather, seasonality, and prior venue changes may shape both awareness and visitation independently of the AI system.

denominator.unit: Spazju Kreattiv venue intervention using forecasted surrounding footfall

site_selection.value: Castille Square was identified as the highest-potential nearby location for outreach because of higher pedestrian flow

staffing_route.value: Guest Relations Officers were deployed at forecasted high-footfall times to inform, direct, and assist passersby with programming, accessibility, and ticketing information

privacy_route.value: The sensors processed video locally and retained anonymized counts and movement patterns without facial recognition or personal-data storage, according to the study

mechanism.value: AI operated as an allocation tool for human cultural mediation: it located likely non-visitors, while staff supplied context and a social invitation that the sensor could not provide

observations.method: Study-reported implementation of AI-recommended staffing shifts informed by continuous footfall monitoring, forecasts, and survey findings.
observations.uncertainty: Only some recommended shifts could be staffed; the case does not provide randomized assignment, a matched control venue, or a complete cost-effectiveness estimate.
observations.subgroup: People passing through Castille Square who were potentially unaware of or uncertain about Spazju Kreattiv's programming and accessibility.
observations.counterinterpretation: Human outreach, special programming, staff availability, and ordinary day-level variation may account for part of the observed change; the AI forecast is not separately identified from the intervention package.

denominator.unit: venue-level comparison of average daily visitors on days with AI-informed staffing recommendations

baseline_visitors.unit: average daily visitors on the study's reference days

intervention_days_visitors.unit: average daily visitors on days when AI-informed staffing recommendations were applied

visitation_change.unit: approximate percent increase in average daily visitation from 55 to 61

outcome_boundary.value: The increase is a venue-footfall outcome, not evidence of repeat attendance, belonging, learning, revenue, demographic diversification, or durable cultural participation

mechanism.value: The case supplies a measurable bridge from data-informed discoverability to physical entry, while leaving the deeper audience relationship open

observations.method: Study comparison of venue benchmarks on days when AI-informed Guest Relations Officer staffing recommendations were implemented; authors call for randomized follow-up.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison is observational, venue-specific, and bundled: it cannot isolate algorithmic forecasting, staff presence, outreach content, timing, programming, or other day-level factors; the article reports footfall rather than long-run participation.
observations.subgroup: Visitors to Spazju Kreattiv during the reported staffing-shift comparison period.
observations.counterinterpretation: The 11% difference may reflect selection of favorable days or concurrent venue conditions; a larger short-term footfall count could coexist with unequal access, superficial visits, or no durable relationship.

related_sources.claim: Open-access article version describing FlowHint sensors, survey methods, AI-informed staffing, and the reported 11% visitation increase.

boundary: This record adds a named cultural-venue episode connecting AI-assisted measurement of non-visitors to human outreach and a venue-level visitation change. It does not establish causal algorithmic impact, equitable participation, revenue, repeat engagement, belonging, or generalizability beyond Spazju Kreattiv.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Peer-reviewed article page and linked open-access version reviewed for the sample, sensor design, survey frame, intervention, reported visitation comparison, privacy claims, and limitations.
